title: UniFi Verified tier (verified.yaml)
description: Intended state the integration API cannot write, asserted against the legacy API by `unifi-reconcile --verify`. Read and reported, never written -- the UI is the write path for everything here. Only declared fields are compared. Keys beginning with an underscore are comments. Secret-named keys are refused before this schema runs.

wan.description: WAN interfaces by name. Not exhaustive: an undeclared WAN is not drift.

auto_link.description: element_adopt.enabled. The UniFi Auto-Link SSID it creates is system-generated, invisible to rest/wlanconf, and can land on the default network (VLAN 1) unnoticed.

enabled_for.description: Which networks the reflector serves. `all` leaves the network list empty; `some` means exactly `networks`.

wifi.description: EXHAUSTIVE. Every SSID the console broadcasts, by any of four views, must be listed here or it is reported as unexpected.

network.description: Network name the SSID maps to. Catches an SSID that has fallen through to the default network.

defaults.description: Per-band expectations applied to every declared access point that has that band. Keys are legacy radio names: ng (2.4 GHz), na (5 GHz), 6e (6 GHz).

access_points.description: EXHAUSTIVE. An adopted AP not listed here is reported as unexpected.

ports.description: Per-port overrides by device MAC and port index, read from stat/device port_overrides (no port profiles exist). Not exhaustive.

label.description: For the human reader; not compared.

reservations.description: EXHAUSTIVE. Every client with use_fixedip on the console must be listed, or it is reported as unexpected.

name.description: The client alias in the UI. Compared when declared; omit for clients that have none.

label.description: For the human reader; not compared.

static_routes.description: EXHAUSTIVE. Every static route on the console must be listed, or it is reported as unexpected. Keyed by name.

name.description: The route name in the UI; the key.

interface.description: interface routes only: the WAN or network name as the UI shows it.

dynamic_dns.description: EXHAUSTIVE. Every Dynamic DNS entry on the console must be listed, or it is reported as unexpected. Keyed by hostname. The password is never declared.

hostname.description: The name the console keeps updated; the key.

service.description: The provider as the console stores it, e.g. afraid, dyndns, cloudflare.

wan.description: The WAN whose address is published, by the name the UI shows, e.g. Internet 1.

server.description: Custom provider server. Empty for a listed provider.

resolves_to_wan.description: Also resolve the hostname from where --verify runs and require that WAN's current address among the answers. Catches a client that stopped updating.

vpn_servers.description: EXHAUSTIVE. Every VPN server network on the console must be listed, or it is reported as unexpected. Keyed by name. Teleport is not a VPN server network and is not listed. Keys are never declared, except peers' public keys.

name.description: The server name in the UI; the key.

subnet.description: The gateway's address in the client range, as the UI shows it, e.g. 192.168.247.1/24.

wan.description: WireGuard: the WAN it listens on, e.g. Internet 1.

zone.description: The firewall zone its clients are in, e.g. Vpn.

client_address.description: WireGuard: the Alternate Address for Clients written into their configuration. null when unset, so clients get the WAN address.

resolves_to_wan.description: Also resolve client_address from where --verify runs and require the listening WAN's current address among the answers.

peers.description: WireGuard. EXHAUSTIVE when present: every peer of this server must be listed. Keyed by name.

public_key.description: The peer's WireGuard public key. Public by design; a change means the peer was recreated.
